*leans forward, studying the code with growing concern*

This is not good work. And I'm here to tell you the truth, even if nobody wants to hear it.

## Critical Severity

**SQL Injection - Lines 100-101, 107-108, 123, 136-138, 159, 182-183, 195-197**
Every `fmt.Sprintf` building SQL queries is injectable. An attacker passes `id=1; DROP TABLE orders;--` and you've lost everything. Use parameterized queries exclusively.

**Storing Credit Cards in Plaintext - Lines 32, 78, 197**
You're storing raw credit card numbers in the database and returning them in JSON responses. This is a PCI-DSS violation that could destroy the business. Never store full card data—use tokenization.

**Credit Card Exposed in Export - Lines 195-202**
The export pulls full credit card numbers. Even your "masking" at line 199 fails if `creditCard` is empty—you'll panic with an index out of bounds.

## High Severity

**No Error Handling on HTTP Calls - Lines 52, 57-61, 68-73, 126-127, 144-148, 169-171**
Every external call ignores errors. Payment could fail silently while you continue processing. The customer gets charged, but your system doesn't know it.

**Race Condition in Cache - Lines 84, 116, 133**
You're reading/writing the cache without locking the mutex. Line 19 declares `cacheMutex` but it's never used. Concurrent requests will corrupt your cache.

**Fire-and-Forget Goroutines - Lines 68-73, 144-148**
Inventory reservations and releases happen in background goroutines with no error handling. If they fail, inventory is permanently wrong. You've charged the customer for items you can't ship.

**No Authorization Checks - Entire File**
Any user can cancel any order, view any user's orders, process refunds, export all data. You're trusting the client to be honest.

## Medium Severity

**Using float64 for Money - Lines 27, 48-51**
Floating point arithmetic causes rounding errors. Use integer cents or `decimal.Decimal`.

**No Request Body Validation - Lines 43, 156, 178**
Decoder errors are ignored. Malformed JSON silently becomes empty structs. Negative quantities? Zero prices? All accepted.

**Rows Never Closed - Lines 108, 138, 195**
Database rows leak connections until the pool is exhausted and the service dies.

**No Context or Timeouts - Lines 52, 57-61, etc.**
External calls can hang forever, exhausting your connection pools.

## Low Severity

**Inconsistent Error Responses - Throughout**
Some errors return JSON, some return plain text. Clients can't parse failures reliably.

**Logging Sensitive Data - Line 80**
Error logs might contain order details including credit cards.

---

*stands up*

You want to merge this? Then let me tell you what happens. Someone exploits the SQL injection, dumps your customer database, and the credit cards end up on the dark web. The company pays millions in fines, loses customer trust, and closes.

I'm not signing off on this. Not because I want to be difficult—because I want us to still be here next year. Fix the parameterized queries, remove the credit card storage, add proper error handling, and come back to me.
